headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[Death toll reaches 1,170]] as six more die in 24 hours
headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,170 as six more die in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports an unprecedented surge in measles deaths, marking the highest number in the country's history.
details: According to the DGHS, six people died from measles symptoms in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 1,170 since March 15. This includes 1,066 deaths from measles symptoms and 104 confirmed cases of measles deaths.

The latest 24-hour report shows 1,074 new cases of measles symptoms and 139 confirmed measles cases. Since March 15, a total of 207,371 people have shown symptoms and over 22,712 have been confirmed positive.
Hospitalizations have been high, with 184,269 patients admitted to hospitals since March 15. Of these, 176,672 patients have recovered and been discharged.

Public health experts attribute the outbreak to extreme negligence in vaccination efforts during 2025, particularly under the interim government. They note that the disease had been largely forgotten for eight years, with infections rarely exceeding 400 cases.

The country had aimed for measles elimination by 2025 and certification of eradication by 2026, but the current crisis has reversed these goals. Experts warn that a lack of attention to the outbreak early in the year and inadequate treatment facilities contributed to the severity.
caption:
1,170 deaths and over 2 lakh cases. Bangladesh is facing its deadliest measles outbreak in history.

According to the DGHS, six people died from measles symptoms in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 1,170 since March 15. This includes 1,066 deaths from measles symptoms and 104 confirmed cases of measles deaths.

The latest 24-hour report shows 1,074 new cases of measles symptoms and 139 confirmed measles cases. Since March 15, a total of 207,371 people have shown symptoms and over 22,712 have been confirmed positive.

Hospitalizations have been high, with 184,269 patients admitted to hospitals since March 15. Of these, 176,672 patients have recovered and been discharged.

Public health experts attribute the outbreak to extreme negligence in vaccination efforts during 2025, particularly under the interim government. They note that the disease had been largely forgotten for eight years, with infections rarely exceeding 400 cases.

The country had aimed for measles elimination by 2025 and certification of eradication by 2026, but the current crisis has reversed these goals. Experts warn that a lack of attention to the outbreak early in the year and inadequate treatment facilities contributed to the severity.
